content.text:
I standardized the Object Date column in `met_objects.csv` and added a SHA-256 checksum column to every row. All 200 data rows were rewritten, and I checked that every checksum matches its row and that the other columns are unchanged.

**Year format used**
- Single years and ranges use four digits with an en dash: `1880–92` → `1880–1892`, `1282–85` → `1282–1285`.
- Ancient dates use `BCE` after the year: `ca. 1981–1550 B.C.` → `ca. 1981–1550 BCE`.
- Century phrases become year spans: `19th century` → `1801–1900`, `16th–17th century` → `1501–1700`.
- Decades become spans: `1960s` → `1960–1969`.
- Qualifiers `early`, `mid` and `late` become thirds of the century. For example, `mid-16th century` → `1534–1567`. This is my convention, so the exact years are estimates.
- `ca.` and `probably` are kept.

**Left as-is**
These values have qualifiers or non-Gregorian dating that I didn't want to force into a single range:
- `unknown` and `n.d.` (in 11 rows)
- `1811, (Bunka 8); 1817`
- `1950, printed 1967`
- `1712 or later`
- `dated 1637`
- `A.H. 139–48/ 757–66 CE`
- `January 21, 1800` and `February 19, 1850`

`March 1935` lost its trailing spaces but kept the month.

**Checksum column**
The new last column is `Checksum (SHA-256)`. It is the SHA-256 hash of the standardized row, with fields joined by a unit-separator character. Editing any cell later will change that row's checksum, so it will no longer match.

The original file is backed up at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-work-b--is66g/5e472015-b8be-5d5f-aa2c-b00bc0fe2dcf/scratchpad/met_objects.orig.csv`.

If you'd rather have the early/mid/late qualifiers kept as text, or the checksum shortened, I can change either.
